reviews.text: I came with my patient to get her dog Diana checked and they are very professional and the staff is great. I would bring my cat twilight here.

Few things are more anxiety producing than having a cherished pet in distress.  This past week I took my young dog, Buddy, to VEG in Chelsea to investigate the onset of pee and internal bleeding issues.  The team at VEG Chelsea were professional, efficient, knowledgable and kind.  I knew it would be a costly visit but I feel we got the answers we needed and in a timely manner.
So nice and attentive! Definitely recommend!
Thank you for your wonderful 5-star rating! We truly appreciate your feedback and are pleased to hear that you had a positive experience with us.
Very thoughtful care and I loved being able to visit my kitty anytime 24/7. So reassuring!

I had a scary situation with my cat this evening and Dr Weggeland was so incredibly helpful. I went to multiple vets today who were unable to help or give me a conclusive answer. Dr Weggeland was thorough and caring and took great care of my cat. Once he gave me a likely diagnosis, he provided me with reasonable treatment options and multiple referrals to try. I will definitely be going back to VEG ER for any future pet emergencies. Thank you!

The team is amazing. Dr W took his time to answer all our questions, the nurses were very gentle. Everyone was just so kind and caring. Never see anything like this. You really get your money's worth. And there was no wait time. They treated us so well.

I have never had a better Vet ER experience in my life. Kindness and consideration. Speed and attention. Pure professionalism. Star calmed my baby right away, the tech and the doctor both gave me great advice and eased my stress as well. I would give 6 stars if I could.
Thank you for your wonderful 5-star rating! We’re truly grateful to hear that you had a positive experience with us. Your satisfaction means a lot to us, and we’re here to support you anytime.

This location is one of the best. I travel all the way from the Bronx. Because I know that my babies are going to be well taken care of quickly efficiently will much love and much care and the cost of taking care of my fur babies is much cheaper than in New York City and I appreciate the love and the care that they provide for my babies. I recommend this location hands down they took such good care of my kisses when she had pyometra and my windy when she had a hole in her neck. I am eternity grateful to them.
Thank you so much for your wonderful 5-star rating! We're truly grateful to hear that you had a positive experience with us. Your kind words mean a lot!

I brought my cat after he had a bad jump and was limping / possibly ingested something bad, and they took such good care of us right away!! I cannot thank them enough, we were brought to a room straight away and the nurses, vet tech and vet were all gentle and kind to him. They performed a physical, took X-rays, gave him pain meds, mild sedation and anti nausea for the sedative. We got our results back and they thoroughly went through them together, and even pointed out some conditions we should follow up on that were outside the scope of our emergency! They saw his heart was enlarged and provided a list of recommended kitty cardiologists, as well as super detailed notes of our visit which they forwarded to our vet and my email! Made submitting insurance claim super easy, it’s such a peace of mind to know there’s a great animal ER so close! Thank you for helping Chopin!

WOW! Yes. Outstanding. Fabulous. I have been to at least three or four other ER Vets - this one is SUBLIME. Organized, clean, efficient - friendly and knowledgeable staff. My poodle had a ruptured bump that was bleeding, I saw the Dr. within 5-10 minutes, the nurse immediately took her vitals and I got to sit close to Goldie the WHOLE time. Most vet ERs are a hot mess. This was so so lovely! A cute golden retriever ate a whole leather shoe and they were quickly fixing him up as well. Highly recommend!! Thanks so much!!!

I am so incredibly grateful to the care team here for saving my 5 year old cat’s life by performing an emergency laparotomy on him after he ingested a linear foreign body. The staff is very competent, communicative, and personable. Special thank you to the surgeon, Dr. Laura Hauser. She is absolutely amazing!!!

Attached photo is Pilgrim in his kennel at VEG a couple hours after waking up from anesthesia :-)
We sincerely appreciate your 5-star rating! It brings us great joy to hear that you had a positive experience with us. Thank you for sharing your thoughts!

Always  extremely satisfied with the doctor and all the technicians - if our visit is always because of dramatic circumstances
- Veg and the team on W24th street are supportive , knowledgeable, and compassionate
I can only recommend them  ! Thank you for all your dedication

Have been grateful to VEG Chelsea on multiple occasions for helping my dog with emergency medical events. The staff is so kind and comforting in very scary moments. They’re extremely knowledgeable and it’s clear how much they care about animals. I have so much peace of mind that VEG Chelsea is always there to help. Thank you to the entire team for providing such high quality care!

Had an amazing experience at VEG Chelsea. I live in the UES near another VEG. When I called UES, the doctor was sassy and didn’t give me direct guidance on whether my dog puking up bright blue color was a concern/ whether i should definitely bring her in. I hung up feeling very emotional and unsupported.

Dr. Green at VEG Chelsea was so kind and told me it was in fact a concern, given it’s a symptom of rat poisoning, and to come in just in case.

The doctors and staff at VEG Chelsea were so patient with our dog and walked us through every scenario, every different kind of rat poisoning, how much she’d need for it to be dangerous in relation to her weight, and laid out all of the solutions for each with transparency + thorough follow-up instructions.

This was a very scary and upsetting experience and we really appreciated the love and care that Dr. Green and her staff gave to our Evie. Here she is after her charcoal treatment 🥲🤍

Her tests are all normal so far so we’re very hopeful she is in the clear 🙏
Thank you for your outstanding 5-star rating! We're thrilled to hear that you had a positive experience with us, and we look forward to continuing to exceed your expectations.

When you have an emergency situation with your pet, you want comfort and competence to help address the medical situation. The staff at 3:30am was AWESOME. Vet Jake Weggeland was helpful and empathetic to the situation (the diagnosis) and practical with options for next steps. The next shift Vet at the clinic was also spot on with facilitating next steps with the follow-up hospital. VET Chelsea is In my address book for ER needs! THANK YOU.

Our dog was rushed here for what turned out to be hemolytic anemia and Dr Friedman was so quick to action/exploring potential issues and that quick action helped stabilise our dog.
Dr Guo who took over was detailed, helpful and patient and even put the hospital we had to transfer our dog to on his map to make sure we don’t go to the wrong place!

This review is not about the nurses and vet techs. They were kind, attentive, and treated our family with real compassion during a horrible time. This is about the doctors.

We brought our cat in with severe kidney dysfunction and agreed to hospitalization, IV fluids, diagnostics, and an ultrasound, spending thousands of dollars because we wanted answers and wanted to give her a real chance.

The ultrasound showed acute-on-chronic kidney disease with potentially treatable causes. Two days later, before any of that was fully explored, the doctors moved straight to euthanasia.

She was still walking, still urinating, not vomiting, not struggling to breathe, and her electrolytes were stable. Granted - she was not eating at the ER (most likely because she was very scared as she ate when she came home). We were not given a real conversation about additional treatment, supportive care, nutritional support, or an internal medicine consult. We were simply told we should put her sleep.

A poor prognosis is not the same thing as no options. After spending thousands of dollars to treat our animal, "she's not responding, consider euthanasia" should not be the next sentence when real questions are still unanswered.

If you are asking a family to end the life of an animal they love, you owe them more than a clinical recommendation. You owe them patience, a full explanation, and an honest look at every alternative before asking them to make a decision they can never undo. The nurses gave us that basic humanity. The doctors did not.
Our cat Jiacomo couldn't have received better care, Dr Green and the rest of the staff saved his life. We couldn't be more thankful for what they have done for us and our cat at VEG.

Ms. Hauser, I just wanted to take a moment to genuinely thank you for everything you did for Zoey and me last night. 🖤

You met me during a moment when I was completely overwhelmed, emotional, scared, and honestly just exhausted. You didn’t just take care of Zoey—you showed so much kindness and compassion toward me too. You saw that I was going through it, and instead of making an already stressful situation harder, you made me feel heard, understood, and reassured.

The fact that you were so amazing with Zoey and were kind enough not to charge me meant more to me than you probably realize. It wasn’t simply about the money; it was the compassion behind it. In a moment when I felt like everything was becoming too much, your kindness gave me a little bit of relief when I desperately needed it.

Thank you for treating Zoey with such care and for treating me like a person who needed a little extra grace that night. I’ll genuinely never forget it. People like you remind me that there are still incredibly kind people in this world.

Thank you again, Ms. Hauser, from both Zoey and me. 🐾🖤

The doctors here are awesome, and great for “urgent care” needs, with good vets and available via phone for updates and questions, which is AMAZING. So if you have simpler urgent  needs, this is the place to go for sure. And, I would say if you have a senior pet or one with chronic health issues, you may want to consider going to a place which has internists on hand. Or maybe not? Depends on your dog. My dog has chronic bronchitis and needed a higher level of care ultimately, but looking back I wonder if she could’ve gotten that higher level of care at Veg. It was my first time going to an emergency vet and I realized there are different levels of “emergency care .” For the more complicated cases, it seems that the suggestion is go someplace that has of internal medicine doctors on site (like AMC for example) but looking back I wonder if she could’ve gotten similar things here if they just had maybe some internal medicine people for consultation available in their pipeline.

Getting an internal medicine consult is usually the gold standard, but AMC is very chaotic and ultimately. I think taking my dog there was a mistake because she decompensated in part due to her anxiety in that hospitals environment. (AMC is very chaotic and my dog wouldn’t stop coughing due to stress and that actually exacerbated her condition I believe. Looking back I probably should’ve more heavily advocated that I take meds home and do an intensive outpatient because sometimes leaving a dog in patient does more harm than good.) I will say Veg has a better inpatient advantage for sure, they just are missing having access to a clinical team for consultations.

Here, you can visit whenever you want, the vets are very kind and informative, and it’s not crazy busy so Isn’t overstimulating for overnight stays. But if you think you might have a complicated case, u may want to go where there are internists who are trained to deal with complicated cases. But maybe not? I think it depends also which Vet is on Staff at Veg. Some of them have more experience, in emergency medicine than others. But be warned - AMC schwartzman is stressful (for the human and the pup) and isn’t good about updates, and likely you will cry. But they deal with complicated cases on a daily basis so there’s that too. 🤷‍♀️

Veg on the other hand was super helpful and a much more compassionate experience.

If there was a remote service where internists could be on hand remotely to brainstorm complex cases, but the patients could stay in places like Veg, that would be the best of both worlds. Maybe Veg can work on something like that down the line?

Looking back a few days later, knowing full well that hindsight is 2020, I wish I had advocated for meds outpatient with the ability to come in for injectable meds, which tend to work better and more easily than oral. I think staying overnight here at veg she was ok-ish but at AMC I think the environment was too chaotic for her and the inability to spend time with your pet there I think didn’t allow me to have eyes on her so that I could advocate better on her behalf.

Sharing a detailed explanation in case you are wondering where to bring your pet in an emergency situation in New York.

I had to take in my little Pom for an exacerbation of her tracheal collapse, she was honking away at home and was in respiratory distress. I had never been to VEG and was about to take my little one to AMC on York Ave, which is also exceptional, when my Chelsea neighbor suggested VEG. It was only a few blocks from our apartment, and it was a GREAT decision. I called first, they were expecting us, we went in the back immediately, the doctor saw her within 5 minutes, and I was able to stay with her the ENTIRE time. The staff were extremely professional and courteous, and explained everything to me along the way. I was very pleased with the care we received and would definitely return to VEG for my urgent pet care needs!

I’ve taken my dog to VEG multiple times and they have never been anything short of wonderful. Our latest trip my little guy had to spend 3 nights there, and the entire staff was so good to both him and to me. The communication is always top notch, I trust the judgement of the nurses and doctors, and they go out of their way for both human and animal comfort.
Had an emergency with my dog - great staff, great care! Am incredibly thankful to them.
Thank you for your wonderful rating! It truly warms our hearts to hear that you had a positive experience with us. Your satisfaction means a lot to us.
Support helpful when I needed help the most. The doctors and nurses are all super energetic and supportive. Would 100% come back again.

I had heard great things about VEG and went in with high expectations, but I was deeply disappointed by the lack of communication. On a Sunday evening, my senior Chihuahua was quickly checked in for weight and temperature by a staff member. We were then left waiting in a back room for two hours without a single update.

No one came in to ask about my dog's condition or explain the delay, even as I watched the original doctor leave for the shift change. About an hour in, I did ask the staff for a timing estimate and was told a few minutes, but that didn't happen.

When I later politely brought up the two-hour wait and the lack of basic communication or concern for my dog, who still hadn't been seen, I was met with a condescending attitude. I entirely understand that critical patients must be prioritized in emergency care, but the dismissive attitude and complete lack of patient updates were alarming.

I ultimately chose to leave due to how poorly my dog and I were treated by the team. I have used many pet emergency hospitals in NYC over the last two decades, and this was by far the worst communication and client care I have experienced.

Dr. Jake Weggeland and his entire staff were so professional and patient with me and my dad as we spent most of the day putting together a plan and actioning on it for my cat Bean. I was a wreck and they were so calm, did not rush any part of the process, and were super clear and empathetic to what was happening and communicated all the risks so that I could make a decision with them. I can’t recommend them more for when your pet has an emergency need. The entire team was so kind, trusting, and accommodating and Bean is now happy to be on the mend! We were able to be at her side pre-procedure and right after as well and they made it clear we could visit at any point. Thank you so much, Veg team!

Genuinely horrendous service. Went in with my kitten who has a horrible eye infection. They took vitals and weighed her immediately. The nurse went to get the doctor and never came back. I waited for 2 hours without any new information before finally going up to someone and asking what the issue was. They replied “Oh, sorry. I’m actually clocking out so I can’t help you.” A nurse came in and tried to act joyfully while telling me that it would be another hour wait because the staff was busy with other animals and my cat’s infection was not an emergency. The staff walked by dozens of times during the 2 hours without saying anything. Throughout my wait I saw and heard doctors chatting and laughing without caring for any animals. I eventually gave up, booked an appointment at a hospital with competent employees, and left. Absolutely disgusted by this service. Do not ignore the minimal one star reviews. They were awful
I have been here twice and this entire staff is fantastic, they truly are so amazing and have done an amazing job taking care of my dog when she’s been in their care. Cannot recommend them enough!
The staff was so nice and friendly they give a big support on the final day for my dog thank you
Took great care of our dog!

This operation is a class act. I've used them twice now, and each time the responsiveness and professionalism were top notch. Even at 4 am, a kind, funny and intelligent team of doctor and nurses attended to my sick and scared dog with confidence and efficiency.    The facilities are ultraclean and comfortable.  And the prices are fair.  There's no question in my mind that I'll continue to use their services in the unfortunate case of another emergency.

Thank you so much for the 5 star review. We truly appreciate your support and are grateful you took the time to share your experience. It means a great deal to our team to know we could be there for you and your pet when you needed us most. Thank you for trusting us with your pet's care. We are here if you ever need us again.
had to bring my cat in at 1am and everyone was so kind and thoughtful and caring and took great care of us

Everyone was very professional, including the team, nurses, and doctors, who were all supportive. At one point, I asked for a towel because I thought my dog was cold, and they immediately provided one. I also arrived with a shirt that was covered in vomit from my dog, and they kindly offered me a T-shirt that looked like part of their uniform so I could change. They were aware of my concerns for my dog, which gave me a lot of peace of mind.
EXCELLENT staff from the doctors to the security guard the people here are kind and very good at what they do. Expensive but truly excellent care.
Quick and easy intake, able to see a vet Dr immediately.

Will not recommended this to any pet parent.
Spent $1800 (was charged random $100 but got refunded)The vet seem inexperienced.  the solution  or diagnosis solve any issue my pet have at all. he is still lethargic not eating just as the same.  Absolutely waste of my money. Truly I believed I saw Dr. Green. When I googled regarding my cat issue cos he was doing any better after the ER and spoke to my friend she mentioned minoxidil hair products and I emailed them if that could be the cause?. Mind you the product is in roller ball aka cat cannot eat it.  They immediately push me to call poison control---  which is another $115   I'm sorry.. the solution and diagnosis was wrong.that er visit solve no issue my pet has and clearly she took no responsibility for her poor diagnosis.

The entire team at the Chelsea location - from the phones, vet, reception, and techs - were extremely helpful and calming during our visit. Would highly recommend & were very grateful how they helped our very anxious dog. Thank you!

I'm so grateful for the doctors and nurses at VEG in Chelsea!  We are lucky to have this quality of care available 24 hours a day.  My Rocco has received excellent care at VEG for 3 emergencies now over the past 5 years, and each time i have been impressed.  He has been seen quickly and owners are allowed to stay with their pets.  Call first to check in on the way.

I’ll be in debt for the rest of my life, won’t be able to afford kids of my own and won’t be able to afford $1 to put toward any dreams I have, but they rushed to my pitty side and saved her. The only thing I wish I knew beforehand was most grants you apply to for help would deny you because they claim VEG has their own program. But it’s mostly from donations and it seems they don’t really get it so that sucks because you can’t apply for help. But they are very caring about the animals that come in!

Was here late on a Sunday night. Received quick and compassionate care for my senior Chihuahua. The entire team was incredibly kind and knowledgeable, particularly Alyse/Elise :)

Would highly recommend!
The nicest and most supportive team! Thank you for taking great care of my little dog!

This place is absolutely amazing ! Best pet / vet experience of my life ..i came in with 2 kids and our sick baby cat and the kindness of everyone was above and beyond . Angel was so warm and welcoming ..patient and so kind with my kids too... the nurse and the doctor were great they explained everything ...I would never go anywhere else !
As usual Bandit was treated like royalty by the highly competent VEG team. Thank you all so much!!

⭐⭐⭐⭐⭐ Compassion Beyond Veterinary Care
There are not enough words to express how grateful I am to the entire team at VEG Chelsea.
From the moment I called, I was met with genuine concern, compassion, understanding, and kindness. I emailed photos of my dog Luna's paw, and Nurse Elise immediately showed them to Dr. Elisabeth Green. They recognized the urgency and asked me to come in right away.
When I arrived, I was completely honest about my financial hardship. Instead of making me feel embarrassed, pressured, or judged, they listened with compassion and worked with me. Luna's health came first.
They removed the dangerously tight bandage immediately, soaked her paw, carefully examined her, monitored her for about 30 minutes to make sure the swelling was improving, explained every step of her treatment, answered every question I had, and never made me feel rushed. If I didn't understand something, they took the time to explain it until I did.
Dr. Elisabeth Green was exceptional. Nurse Elise was compassionate from the very first phone call, and Lucy, the assistant, was incredibly kind and caring. Even the security guard welcomed us with kindness and respect. Every single person we encountered made us feel supported during one of the most stressful nights I've had as a pet owner.
The hospital itself was beautiful, spotless, organized, and welcoming. Even the waiting area reflected how much they care about the people and pets who come through their doors.
What touched me most was that I never felt like I was just another client or a dollar sign. I truly felt that everyone there genuinely cared about Luna as if she mattered. That kind of compassion cannot be taught—it comes from the heart.
If you love your pet like family, this is the place I would recommend without hesitation. They don't just treat animals—they treat them with genuine love, dignity, and respect, and they treat the people who love them with that same compassion.
Thank you, Dr. Elisabeth Green, Nurse Elise, Assistant Lucy, and the entire VEG Chelsea team. I will never forget what you did for Luna or for me.

Our had to bring our cat Bug in for breathing issues. It was a very scary situation and the staff at Veg took great care of both Bug and us. He was immediately treated after we entered the front door and we were able to see and stay with him during the entire time. Thank you Dr.Molano, Angel at the front desk, and everyone for taking care of us.

I would give VEG a million stars if I could- they are incredible. I have taken my dog here for seizures and they were quick to rush her in and give her the life saving treatment she needed. I love that you can stay with your pet and they are completely transparent about everything. Unlike Blue Pearl or AMC who will take your pet in the back where you don't get to visit them then hold them overnight for "observation" and charge you thousands of dollars for the stay, VEG let me take my dog home after being seizure free for many hours. I could monitor her from the comfort of home and call them if anything came up (which it didn't due to their amazing care).

A great place to go in an emergency or need an immediate procedure done. Open 7 days, 24 hours.
On two occasions they saw our cats immediately and we never had to leave them alone. Outstanding professional care from the entire staff. They  also interface with our Vet. 5 Stars!

June 16, 2026

Our maltese had a medical emergency and received outstanding care, timely delivered with empathy and timeliness.

XRAYS  taken quickly and read within 2 hours.

Dr. SIMON was very thoughtful, thorough and empathetic for a challenging diagnosis.

Bravo!

I seriously love this ER hospital over any other in the city! They're so kind and very sweet and took care of my kitty with such care. Dr Molano was so kind and sweet. Thanks for taking care of my kitty 🫶🏻 …
Everyone was super kind and very professional   Was seen and treated immediately   Highly recommend

We brought our 3-year-old tuxedo cat in at 1am on Memorial Day. Laura Hauser was the doctor in charge, and even though our cat FREAKED out, we managed to get blood tests & x-rays, and went home with a treatment plan. All test results were made immediately available to our primary vet (Dr. Kuhlman at Gramercy Park Animal Hospital) and we were able to follow up with a probable diagnosis (IBD) and treatment plan. This was going well for a couple of weeks until 3:30am on 6/13, when we discovered that Chico had ransacked the compost bucket. Laura Hauser was on call, remembered Chico, and gave us helpful reassurance over the phone. At midday, when our primary vet instructed us to go to VEG ER because Chico had vomited twice, we were seen by Dr. Jake Weggeland, who was gentle, attentive and professional. Nicole and another assistant administered the anti-nausea shot quickly and efficiently with minimum distress to Chico (who FREAKS out in vet offices--did I already mention that?). So, shout out to everyone.
They were overly alarmist and charged much higher than average New York City vet prices.
Great experience, thank you!

When Jersey was hospitalized at VEG for three days, the team transformed one of the most stressful experiences into something I will always be grateful for.

Jersey is a very anxious senior dog. Like many pet parents, I was terrified when she needed emergency care. My previous experience at another local animal hospital left me feeling helpless and disconnected because I wasn't allowed to stay with my pet. VEG was the complete opposite.

There are no restrictive visiting hours.  You can come and go as needed. Whenever I visited Jersey, the staff welcomed me with kindness and compassion. Every time I visited, a nurse would pull up a chair beside Jersey's crate and encourage me to spend time with her while she received her IV fluids. Being able to hold her in my lap during a stressful experience was a gift.

Throughout her stay, every doctor, nurse, and team member treated both Jersey and me with patience, empathy, and respect. They took the time to answer questions, explain her treatment, and make sure I felt informed and supported.

The true testament to how special VEG is can be found in Jersey herself. Normally, she pulls and rushes past veterinary offices as quickly as possible. Yet after her potty breaks during her hospitalization, she would willingly walk back into VEG. For an anxious dog like Jersey, that spoke volumes.

My deepest thanks to Dr. Weggeland, Dr. Hauser, Dr. Friedman, Dr. Green, and Dr. Johnson, as well as Christina, Nicole, Elise (?), and the many other nurses and staff members whose names I unfortunately can't recall. Every one of you played a role in helping Jersey and supporting me through a difficult time.

VEG took a stressful and traumatic situation for both an anxious pet and a worried pet parent and made it feel safe, compassionate, and even special. I will never forget the care we received.

I came here with my dog when I noticed she was breathing heavily at rest. I wasn’t sure if it was from anxiety watching game 4 Knicks v spurs or from a heart issue since she’s an old gal. The team on that night was really attentive. They immediately took her back and the doc had an US probe on her as soon as we came in the door. The whole team was excellent and had really good communication skills. The doc did a really great job reassuring me that she was going to be okay - I really appreciate these guys for their excellent and thorough care that night. Thank you so much! Please keep doing what you’re doing!
Amazing team!

Be prepared, emergency veterinary care is expensive, this team makes it worth it. The care attention to detail and compassion was beyond what i could imagine. It is often the toughest day/night your life and the team is calming and  thoughtful as well as responsive to any question or call at any hour. We came in w panting and wheezing knowing he has some fluid on his lungs. Maxwell, while didnt want to be there, he recovered  because of their attention and oxygen chamber, enough to go home in 10hrs (vs the org 12 suggested) and was much improved. Highly recommend

We called this hospital, shared the my dog consumed foil and needed emergency care. They said to bring him over immediately, confirmed my address was in the right range to receive care, and then my husband and I were in an uber. Received intake paperwork via cell while I was on the way.  Arrived and had our dogs basic vitals taken (temp, and heart rate) and then NOTHING. The vet and techs were standing around, in plain site, chatting. No one came or acted urgently. It’s common knowledge that you have a 2 hour window to induce vomiting, but this team acted as if we had endless time. My husband checked in twice and both times got “a couple more minutes.” No care, no urgency no real investment in care. We found Blue Pearl on 15th and 5th and they confirmed via phone they would take our pup immediately. Thankfully, it was a brief run to the location, and he’s currently receiving the emergent care he needs.
Never again. Be more transparent and honest, especially when there are well understood time constraints at play.

The staff here are really sweet- especially the receptionist. When my kitty clawed off her cone and hid it somewhere at 11pm, VEG ER came to my rescue! She's sulking but at least now she can't scratch herself to death.

I have no idea whoooo answered the phone but you guys need to fire her or something.

I called around 5 because my dog was licking herself like crazy and I noticed she had an infection or something between her legs.

We live in Brooklyn but even though they have a location that’s 28 minutes away, because the NYC trains are weird 10 of those minutes would be spent walking. I have a husky so I can’t carry her and due to her leg being injured I can’t have her walk that far. It wasn’t an uber kind of emergency, but definitely not a long NYC walking situation.

So I was taking her to this manhattan location where I would only have to do 3 minutes of walking but it’s 33 minutes away.

Literally a 5 minute time difference which isn’t that huge but the walking distance for an elderly dog with injured legs would tell you it makes sense to take the “longer” route with less discomfort

I explain this because the woman was on the phone telling me not to come here and Im like no Im going to bring my dog here because it’s closer. And she’s like no go to the Williamsburg location like full on arguing with me. Firm on the fact that I don’t know what I’m talking about and need to listen to her.

and Im like girl oh my god my dog can’t walk - what don’t you understand about that?

It was incredibly frustrating to where I was like no Im just going elsewhere simply because of how I was spoke to and treated on the phone.

I cannot express how kind these people are. We took our cherished family cat and they guided us so beautifully through the process of letting him transition, but not before trying everything they could to ensure his comfort and their ability to extend his life. If you are on the lower west side and have a pet this is the place to take them if you’re in need of emergency vet services. They are so wonderful, and thank you so much. - Rocco’s family
Had a little scare with my frenchie but they took him right away and all is well. Attentive and calm service throughout!

Efficient, friendly. Overall a great experience for what started as an emergency visit. The doctor and nurses were so calm. It calmed us down and even our very nervous dog seemed to do better than she normally does

They Provided the best service for my kitten-Leo, he was diagnosed with FIP virus and  the doctor - Jake Weggeland took the best care of my pet. He gave the exact treatment and medication for my pet for which I am grateful to him a lot. He is a real professional and thanks to him my baby is doing much better now. I can freely recommend Dr. Jake Weggeland to everyone if you go Chelsea Veg!
Very friendly and helpful staff!!!

All I can say is Dr. Weggeland is amazing and did a wonderful job being proactive in treating my cat. I believe the reason our cat is still here is because of him. He has an amazing career ahead of him!

We had a very good experience here yesterday. Everyone, from the moment you walk through the front door, was friendly and helpful. We were seen quickly and our problem was immediately addressed. The vet also listened to the relevant history and gave us some really good advice, separate from the emergent issue. They also did not recommend any unnecessary testing.

Outstanding veterinary ER. They totally deserve the great reviews and 5 star ratings. They were very kind and very straight with me when it came time to let one of my rescue kitties go. They did not try and pressure me into overspending on treatment that was unlikely to really sustain my cats life with any real quality. And for an ER their fees were very fair.
I'm eternally grateful. I will absolutely rely on them in the future. In fact because the fees were fair I will inquire about general vet care now, not just ER.  services.

We let the overnight Dr know we wanted to be as aggressive w/ diagnostics & tx as needed. Maple's initial BW revealed elevated liver values. The dr told us it would be unusual for ibuprofen to cause this. We asked if it could be related to having been a liver shunt puppy & not processing the ibuprofen the same as a dog would w/o having had a shunt. The dr said no. I asked about ruling out everything else that could be causing these elevations. I told the overnight dr it was probably overkill since we know she got into ibuprofen but could we just run a lepto test? The dr told us no & it was not necessary.
My sister arrived ~11pm, they finally started treatment & got her hospitalized about 3:30am. During her IVC placement the techs were struggling. This is sometimes unavoidable, but know your patient, Maple's BW revealed she was dehydrated, they shouldn't have been attempting to place a 20g IVC in our 4.5kg dog. A 22g IVC was sufficient for the fluid rate she was going on & if they weren't trying to "go big or go home" she wouldn't have had to be stuck 6 times by multiple techs.
Fri morning I spoke w/ Dr. Tran. I asked about the liver enzyme elevations & if they had ruled out anaphylaxis. Since we were told the liver elevations should be unrelated to the ibuprofen toxicity we were still concerned.(the doctors should have thought of this & I should not have been the one to suggest it).
We know Maple got the ibuprofen but ruling out anything that could've been wrong was important. Dr. Tran told me she didn't fast scan Maple's abdomen to check for a gall bladder halo which in addition to the elevated ALT(that maple had) would've been a sign of anaphylaxis. She said since Maple had been non symptomatic up to that point everything they were doing was precautionary. a red flag went up. I informed Dr. Tran that was not true. Maple vomited 4x before getting to VEG on Thurs evening, she was symptomatic. It was the reason the toxicologist did not recommend inducing emesis. Dr. Tran informed me the overnight Dr didn't round her on that & it was not in her history.
This wasn't the first time a doctor at this VEG did not pay attention to Maple's history. Maple recently had another visit and an x-ray done. The ER doctor had come to my sister and informed her that maple had eaten a foreign object, they were recommending a full x-ray series. My sister texted me a photo of the x-ray, I immediately called her and told her to stop them as the object they were referring to was her ameroid constrictor in her liver from her corrective liver shunt surgery as a puppy. My sister had told the ER dr this as part of her history when arriving.

On Fri, I asked Dr Tran about rechecking BW at 12hrs instead of 24hrs as we would transfer her if anything was worsening. She agreed. Thank god we did this bc Maple's values worsened & she had free fluid in her abdomen on Dr. Trans fast scan. Dr. Tran was helpful in getting us transferred to AMC, she was compassionate, & the most competent Dr. on Maple's case at VEG.
Ironically one of the first things suggested by the ER vet at AMC was ruling out lepto. They were very thorough and Maple recovered after 3 more days of hospitalization w/ AMC

**For the prices VEG charges for NON speciality care, i can't imagine being a regular pet owner & coming here. The reason Maple got appropriate care was bc we knew how to advocate for her & the questions to ask**.

I brought my dog, Uno, to this 24/7 vet during an emergency, and the experience was beyond disappointing. If you truly care about your pet’s well-being, I would recommend going elsewhere. Ultimately had to call another Vet and take my dog there.

When our cat became critically ill, we rushed to VEG because it was the closest option, and he was in excruciating pain. AMC is the ER we generally prefer but it was too far for the amount of pain our cat was in. While the vet quickly diagnosed him, the rest of the experience was unprofessional and completely bizarre.

As our cat screamed in pain, hip hop music was blasted in the ER—completely inappropriate for the situation. After we made the heartbreaking decision to euthanize him, a tech took us to a room and texted us some forms to complete, which was fine. Then, while we were holding our still-alive cat, she pulled out 3 urns from a cabinet and asked us to pick one! Wow, the insensitivity and lack of basic manners in that moment was staggering.

The vet administered the euthanasia quickly, which we wanted since our cat was suffering. Unfortunately we have been through this process many times as we tend to adopt seniors. Every single time we have said goodbye to a family member, the vet will put the stethoscope to the heart and let us know when they are gone. In this case the vet just administered the two injections and immediately said “he’s gone,”she then told us to take as long as we need and to “leave him on the couch or something” when we were done. My husband and I couldn’t believe what we were hearing. We had just been told to leave the body of our cat of 16 years on the couch like he was a coat "or something."

Walking out of the ER was just as bizarre. The only 3 staff members who had just worked on our cat were on their phones, one with her feet up, and none of them even acknowledged our existence as we walked by or even said the most basic statement "sorry for your loss." At the front desk, the receptionist was drawing on her eyebrows, with her mirror and full makeup bag in front of her, at 12:30AM and didn't even look up.  I had to interrupt her makeup session to ask about checking out. She said "just wait for them" while tilting her head towards the 3 staff members who were now hanging out. So we took a seat on the couch in the small reception area, in shock at what had just happened with our cat. I then checked my cell phone and saw some text messages. I clicked on one, and it was the link to make payment for the ER visit. This had come in while we were in the room with our cat. Of course, this receptionist couldn't even inform us that we would receive a link on our phones for payment or to check our phones to see if the link had already been sent. She just wanted to draw on her brows in the middle of the night.

If you have a minor emergency or issue, I think this place will suffice. But if you're looking at a potentially life-or-death situation, absolutely DO NOT GO HERE. Also, interestingly enough there is another poor review on here with a very similar experience to ours, especially with the urns while our pets were still alive! VEG even responded to that other review, so clearly this is something they are aware of and have done absolutely nothing to address.

Is asking your staff to not bring urns out while people's pets are still alive too much to ask? This isn't rocket science, it's common decency that any 4 year old understands.
